comment: PACT Identity conformance suite (PACT 1.0, spec sections 2, 3, 4 and 6), for both roles: a Provider that hosts businesses' agents and a personal-agent platform that calls them. Every requirement is one MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD or MAY line of https://openpactprotocol.org/spec.md, quoted in `rule` and kept in the spec's order, with a `check` a program can run. The claim vectors in `jwt_vectors` are checkable with no network and no clock: each case carries its own `now`, and the runner signs each case with the test key below unless the case names another signer. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY for AgentMesh's code (the PACT Provider in services/src/pact-provider/, beside the A2A gateway, and the personal-agent side in services/src/pact/): when a test against it fails, fix the code, and change the fixture only with the spec. Where PACT's reference conformance suite (openpactprotocol/openpactprotocol e2e/pact.test.ts at 838c6bd) disagrees with the spec, the case says so in `reference_differs` and docs/pact-working-group-notes.md carries the question.
spec: PACT 1.0, https://openpactprotocol.org/spec.md sections 2, 3, 4, 6 (profile PACT Identity, section 7)

test_key.comment: TEST VECTOR. A throwaway ES256 key for the claim vectors; it controls nothing and is registered nowhere real. The runner registers it at the provider under test as issuer `https://pa.test.invalid` with audience `https://provider.test.invalid/a2a`.

requirements.rule: Requests SHOULD send `A2A-Version: 1.0` and `Content-Type: application/json`.
requirements.check: Every request the personal agent sends to a Provider carries both headers.

requirements.rule: A2A responses MUST use `Content-Type: application/a2a+json`.
requirements.check: message:send, GET tasks and every A2A error envelope answer with Content-Type application/a2a+json.

requirements.rule: One card per Brand, served at `GET {PROVIDER_URL}/a2a/{brandId}/.well-known/agent-card.json`, with no authentication.
requirements.check: The card of a known brand is 200 with no Authorization header.

requirements.rule: An unknown `brandId` gets `404` with no A2A body.
requirements.check: GET /a2a/unknown-brand/.well-known/agent-card.json is 404 and its Content-Type is not application/a2a+json.

requirements.rule: The card MUST list a `supportedInterfaces` entry with `protocolBinding: "HTTP+JSON"` and `protocolVersion: "1.0"`. Its `url` is the interface URL.
requirements.check: supportedInterfaces holds an entry with those two values, and every other route in this suite hangs off its url.

requirements.rule: The card MUST declare the personal-agent JWT as an `httpAuthSecurityScheme` with `scheme: "Bearer"`, `bearerFormat: "JWT"`, listed alone in one `securityRequirements` entry.
requirements.check: securitySchemes has a scheme of that shape, and securityRequirements has an entry naming that scheme and nothing else.
requirements.reference_differs: The spec names the scheme paJwt in its examples; the reference suite reads securitySchemes.platformJwt. The name is not normative. AgentMesh names it paJwt.

requirements.rule: The personal agent gets the card URL from the Brand; it never builds it from a Brand ID.
requirements.check: The personal agent's send call takes a card URL (or the Brand's own domain, whose /.well-known/agent-card.json it fetches) and has no form that takes a brandId.

requirements.rule: Personal agents pick the interface by binding and version, not by position.
requirements.check: Given a card whose first supportedInterfaces entry is JSONRPC and whose second is HTTP+JSON 1.0, the personal agent sends to the second.

requirements.rule: `POST message:send` answers `200` with `{ "message": Message }` (or `{ "task": Task }` under section 5.5).
requirements.check: A valid message gets 200 and a body with exactly one of message or task.

requirements.rule: `GET tasks` answers `200` with an empty `ListTasksResponse` (`pageSize` 1 to 100, default 50).
requirements.check: GET tasks?pageSize=20 is {tasks:[], nextPageToken:"", pageSize:20, totalSize:0}; GET tasks gives pageSize 50; pageSize=0 and pageSize=101 are INVALID_PARAMS.

requirements.rule: `GET tasks/{id}` and `POST tasks/{id}:cancel` answer `TASK_NOT_FOUND`.
requirements.check: Both answer 404 with reason TASK_NOT_FOUND after a valid token.

requirements.rule: Other A2A operations behave as A2A defines.
requirements.check: With streaming false: POST message:stream and POST tasks/{id}:subscribe are UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION. With extendedAgentCard false: GET extendedAgentCard is UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION. With pushNotifications false: GET and POST tasks/{id}/pushNotificationConfigs, and GET and DELETE tasks/{id}/pushNotificationConfigs/{configId}, are PUSH_NOTIFICATION_NOT_SUPPORTED.

requirements.rule: Any route that isn't an A2A operation gets `404` or `405` with no A2A body.
requirements.check: With no token: GET unknown, GET/PUT/DELETE message:send, POST tasks, DELETE tasks/{id}/pushNotificationConfigs and POST tasks/{id}/pushNotificationConfigs/{configId} are 404 or 405 and not application/a2a+json.

requirements.rule: Routing happens before authentication; an unknown Brand is `404` even with a valid token.
requirements.check: GET /a2a/missing-brand/tasks with a valid token is 404 with no A2A body.
requirements.reference_differs: Section 3.4 says Providers SHOULD authenticate before looking up the Brand. AgentMesh reads routing as matching the path: path, then authentication, then the Brand, as the reference does.

requirements.rule: The Provider keeps, per personal agent, `issuer` (exact string match against `iss`), `jwksUri` (HTTPS), and enabled.
requirements.check: A registration can be looked up by issuer and gives its JWKS URL and its enabled state; an issuer that differs by one character (a trailing slash) is not found.

requirements.rule: Providers MAY disable a personal agent; its requests then get `401`.
requirements.check: After the test issuer is disabled, a request with a valid token from it is 401; after it is enabled again, 200.

requirements.rule: `audience` is one value per Provider and MUST NOT be derived from a card URL.
requirements.check: The Provider's audience is one configured string, the same for every brand; a token whose aud is a brand's interface URL is 401.

requirements.rule: The personal agent puts the Provider's assigned `audience` in `aud` verbatim; it MUST NOT derive it from a card URL.
requirements.check: The personal agent's aud for a Provider comes from its record of that Provider; a card from a Provider it has no record of is refused with a plain reason, not sent with a guessed audience.

requirements.rule: Every request except the card carries `Authorization: Bearer <pa-jwt>`; a request without it is refused.
requirements.check: GET tasks with no Authorization is 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="a2a" and no A2A body; so is POST message:send with no token and a body of `{`.

requirements.rule: `alg` is `ES256` or `RS256`. Providers MUST reject others.
requirements.check: jwt_vectors cases alg_hs256 and alg_none are refused; alg_es256 and alg_rs256 are accepted.

requirements.rule: `kid` SHOULD match a key in the JWKS.
requirements.check: Every token the personal agent signs has a kid that its published JWKS lists.

requirements.rule: `iss` MUST equal the registered issuer.
requirements.check: jwt_vectors case iss_unregistered is refused.

requirements.rule: `sub` MUST be present. Stable, opaque, per User. MUST NOT contain personal data.
requirements.check: Provider: jwt_vectors cases sub_missing and sub_empty are refused. Personal agent: the sub for one person is the same on every request to one Provider, and contains no name, email, account id or handle (it is a digest).

requirements.rule: `aud` MUST equal the assigned audience. One string.
requirements.check: jwt_vectors cases aud_wrong and aud_array are refused.

requirements.rule: `iat` MUST be present. Reject if more than 30 s in the future.
requirements.check: jwt_vectors cases iat_missing and iat_31s_future are refused; iat_30s_future is accepted.

requirements.rule: `exp` MUST be present and at most 300 s after `iat`.
requirements.check: Provider: jwt_vectors cases exp_missing and exp_301s are refused, exp_300s is accepted. Personal agent: every token it signs has exp minus iat of at most 300.

requirements.rule: `jti` MAY be present. Providers need not track replay.
requirements.check: A token without jti is accepted, and the same token is accepted twice and at two brands.

requirements.rule: Providers MUST verify the signature via `jwksUri`, allow at most 30 s clock skew, and reject unknown or disabled personal agents.
requirements.check: jwt_vectors cases bad_signature, unknown_kid_other_key, expired_31s and iss_unregistered are refused; expired_29s is accepted (AgentMesh allows the full 30 s); a disabled issuer is refused (PI-R2).

requirements.rule: The User is the pair `(personal agent, sub)`; the personal agent MUST reuse the same `sub` for the same User.
requirements.check: Two sends for one person to one Provider, minutes apart and after a restart, carry the same sub.

requirements.rule: Every authentication failure answers `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="a2a"` and no A2A body.
requirements.check: Each refused jwt_vectors case is exactly that response.

requirements.rule: Providers SHOULD authenticate before looking up the Brand or reading the body.
requirements.check: POST message:send with no token and an unparseable body is 401, not INVALID_PARAMS.

requirements.rule: The request is an A2A `SendMessageRequest`; `configuration` and `metadata` MAY be ignored.
requirements.check: A message with configuration and metadata set is answered as if they were absent.

requirements.rule: `role` MUST be `ROLE_USER`. `parts` MUST have at least one non-blank `text` part. Other part kinds get `CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED`.
requirements.check: role ROLE_AGENT is INVALID_PARAMS; parts [{text:"  "}] is INVALID_PARAMS; parts [{raw:"aGVsbG8="}] is CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED; a body of `{` is INVALID_PARAMS.

requirements.rule: `taskId` MUST be absent; otherwise `TASK_NOT_FOUND`.
requirements.check: A message carrying taskId is 404 with reason TASK_NOT_FOUND.

requirements.rule: `messageId` MUST be unique within the context.
requirements.check: The personal agent mints a fresh messageId per new message and reuses one only to retry the same message.

requirements.rule: The reply is synchronous: `{ "message": Message }` with `role: ROLE_AGENT` and `contextId` set (or a task, section 5.5).
requirements.check: A first message gets a ROLE_AGENT message with a contextId and no taskId.

requirements.rule: Without `contextId`, the message starts a new conversation and the Provider mints an opaque `contextId`. With `contextId`, the message continues that conversation.
requirements.check: Two messages sent with the first reply's contextId get replies carrying that same contextId, and the second is answered in the light of the first.

requirements.rule: The context MUST belong to this Brand and this `(personal agent, sub)`; otherwise `INVALID_PARAMS`, without saying whether it exists for someone else.
requirements.check: A contextId used by another sub at the same brand, or by the same sub at another brand, is 400 INVALID_PARAMS with the message "Unknown contextId", the same answer as a contextId that never existed.

requirements.rule: `contextId` is state, not a credential. Ordinary turns create no A2A Task.
requirements.check: After ordinary turns, GET tasks is still empty and no reply carries a task.

requirements.rule: A Provider MAY close a conversation. A message to a closed `contextId` gets `UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION`.
requirements.check: After the provider closes a context, a message to it is 400 UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION.

requirements.rule: On a closed conversation, the personal agent starts a new conversation by omitting `contextId`.
requirements.check: After UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION on a context, the personal agent's next send to that brand carries no contextId and records the new one.

requirements.rule: A repeated `messageId` in the same `contextId` returns the stored reply without re-running the agent. If there is no stored reply yet, return `INVALID_PARAMS`.
requirements.check: The same message sent twice gets replies with the same messageId and the agent runs once; a repeat while the first is still running is INVALID_PARAMS.

requirements.rule: A2A errors use the A2A / AIP-193 envelope. `code` repeats the HTTP status; the reason is `error.details[0].reason`.
requirements.check: Every error in this suite has error.code equal to the HTTP status, error.status as in the table, and details[0] {"@type":"type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo", reason, domain:"a2a-protocol.org"}.

requirements.rule: Clients MUST NOT infer the reason from the status alone.
requirements.check: The personal agent decides what to do from details[0].reason: a 400 with UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION starts a new context, and a 400 with INVALID_PARAMS does not.

requirements.rule: `429` with `Retry-After` when a Provider rate-limits a personal agent or a `(personal agent, sub)`.
requirements.check: Past the provider's per-user limit, message:send is 429 with a Retry-After header in seconds.

requirements.rule: On `429`, personal agents SHOULD wait `Retry-After` before retrying.
requirements.check: Given 429 with Retry-After: 2, the personal agent's retry comes at least 2 seconds later, or it reports the wait to its caller instead of retrying.

jwt_vectors.comment: Claims checks for section 3.2, run against the verifier with the test key registered. `now` is seconds since the epoch. A case's `header` and `claims` are signed as given unless `sign` says otherwise: `hs256` signs with the shared secret "not-an-allowed-key", `none` sends an empty signature, `other_key` signs with a fresh key whose kid is not published, `rs256` signs with a fresh RSA key published in the test JWKS beside the EC key.
